title: The Sick Village
timelinePosition: Two days' ride south of Millhaven (Ch3 closed on the evening of the first day, at the farm with the lit shrine). Arrival late morning; infirmary work through the afternoon; the join at late afternoon; the granary at dusk; the initiate dies in the evening; the shutdown and the ward vigil run through the night; morning departure. Jaina has slept in camp at least once since she slept in the saddle, so she arrives sharp, and the night vigil wears her down again. Mark time by events, not counts (Jaina voice rule).
openLocation: A working village south of Millhaven where people are falling ill but have not named the outbreak
transport: Southbound on Thalassian horses, then on foot inside the village
immediateObjective: Learn how the sickness gets into people quickly enough to keep this village from becoming another Millhaven.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Jaina; nothing she could not perceive or infer
No grain connection before Jaina earns it from the patient pattern (B5); bread smoke and the bakery before then are ambient texture only
No proof of a cult before the granary scene (B8)
No solved old carter mystery; the carter and the newer grain man stay unconnected scraps, and the supplier description in B7 is a resemblance, not an identification
Jaina is never clueless about necromancy: her gap is banned practice, not the field itself

Jaina's narration name for Sylvanas moves from 'Windrunner' (her Ch2 narration: 'Windrunner', 'the Ranger-General', once 'the elf') to 'Sylvanas' across the chapter. The slide comes after B2 and should settle by Scene 3. Aloud she keeps saying 'Ranger-General' all chapter; she does not say 'Sylvanas' aloud yet. She stops talking down to her, and there is no open emotional trust.
Lyriel's switch from 'Lady Proudmoore' to 'Jaina' lands in the knot lesson (B4)
No Barov connection and no concrete recognition of the old carter
Neral and the fourth ranger are gone; the party is exactly four and the empty places are a callback, not a new image
Fatigue from the Ch 2 no-sleep ride has been partly slept off, but the chapter's night work should tire her again
Brask appears last on page here; do not return him

Custody terms from Ch2 still hold: Jaina is a prisoner in the middle of the line. In the village Sylvanas works in pairs (her Ch3 drill), so Lyriel stays with Jaina in the infirmary and Cyndia goes with Sylvanas. The pairing is the custody arrangement, and Jaina may notice it as one.

Jaina's hands are the running cost: as of Ch3 the left is raw and wrapped in linen, the right has been dead since the Ch2 frost-sheet, and Sylvanas banned hand-reading. Do not heal them off-page. Body reads go through spell light and the staff, not deep palm reads. The B9 barrier and the night vigil cost her more, and nothing resets.
Andorhal has never been named on the page. Its first mention needs an in-world source (see B7 and B11a), not a guess from nowhere.
The village stays unnamed (the outline and Brask's voice sheet give it no name). If the writer names it, the memory-keeper must log the name for Brask's Ch23 letter.
Brask's voice-sheet sample 'I sold barley in Millhaven last autumn' is a grain pre-signal; do not use it before B5. In B2 he repeats 'Millhaven.' and nothing grain-related.

Neral already rode north with the survivor girl and the warning
The old carter on the road and the girl's newer grain man are still only weak clues

Proof of a cult before the granary scene
That Jaina knows nothing about necromancy
Concrete recognition of the old carter's identity
Open emotional trust between Jaina and Sylvanas
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Grain carries the plague into people
Roads and storehouses are how the plague spreads

pov: She opens believing that if she can find the entry route fast enough, she can stop this village from becoming another Millhaven.
She keeps reaching for a clean magical answer and underrates Sylvanas's read of people, habits, and supply.
By the end, Jaina has the answer, but it comes through food, labor, timing, and Sylvanas's practical eye as much as through spellwork.
She stops treating Sylvanas like escort muscle and starts bringing the human side of the problem straight to her.
She leaves with a village that lives because they were on time, and with a ranger's knot in her hands that Lyriel taught her.

beats: Jaina starts out reading Sylvanas as sharp, useful, and secondary to the real magical problem.
Sylvanas keeps seeing the pressure points Jaina misses: fear, routine, authority, and supply.
By the end, Jaina is thinking of her as Sylvanas, not just the ranger, and she stops talking down to her.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They enter the village as two specialists on the same road, but not the same method.
The investigation proves neither approach works alone.
They leave still tense, but now they are solving one problem together instead of arguing over whose kind of knowledge counts.
This is their one clean win: on time, and it holds.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the riding party.
Lyriel: still with the riding party. She works the infirmary beside Jaina and teaches her the Farstrider one-handed bandage knot.
Neral: not with the party. She already left north with the survivor girl.

Captain Willem Brask: the village militia captain. He blocks them, yields to Sylvanas, and stops the grain on their word. He does not return on-page. His only later appearance is a sworn letter for the defence in Chapter 23.
Local village cast: the medic, granary keeper, and cult initiate belong to this outbreak site only.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 5 opens with the same four riders following the grain road southwest.

factsLocked: Grain is confirmed as the plague carrier.
The village lives. Captain Willem Brask stopped the grain on their word and wrote their names in his ledger.
Jaina can tie the Farstrider one-handed knot Lyriel taught her.
Roads and storehouses are how the plague spreads.
A live watcher existed inside the village and died by poison rather than talk.
The party's next move is to follow the route southwest toward Andorhal.
Millhaven remains the first village fully claimed in the pattern, while other settlements are still in earlier stages.
The old carter and the survivor's newer grain man remain weak but persistent clues.
factsNotEarned: Concrete recognition of the old carter's identity.
Open emotional trust between Jaina and Sylvanas.

scenes.title: The Village Before Collapse
scenes.sceneFunction: They enter a village that still looks functional, and Jaina has to prove the plague is already inside it.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Two days' ride south of Millhaven, four riders where seven came down from the Pass: Neral, the fourth ranger and the girl went north with the dispatch. Jaina knows what she did at Millhaven (the well, the storehouse she refused to call the origin, the girl in the cellar, the count in the cow way) and what she heard on the road: the carter's question about a young grain-man, the girl's newer grain seller, the sickness reading 'wider' ahead. She does not know about Sylvanas's palm on the noon stone or that Sylvanas saw her circle on the map. Contamination is physical, active in living flesh before death, and in water and soil; the entry route is unknown. Hands wrapped, hand-reading banned. Custody terms hold. She reads Sylvanas as sharp and useful on maps and ground, and secondary to the magical problem when it comes to people.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina assumes the problem is hers and magical; Sylvanas solves the first obstacle with no magic at all.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only (plague-mechanism.md: contamination enters the gut first, then the wider system; thalassian-horses.md: tack and horse cues). Village layout (lane, infirmary, bakery within sight) is planner inference; the outline gives the village no name and Brask has no supporting.md entry. General historical analogue, not searched: bread-borne contamination in medieval villages presenting as ordinary fever.

beats.goal: Read the village on arrival: find the necromantic wrongness under ordinary life and decide whether it is already rooted here.
beats.conflict: Everything looks functional. Market noise, bread smoke and people acting normal bury the signal; Jaina's sense has to be sorted from the weather of a working place, and before she can move the militia captain stops the party in the lane.

outcome.summary: She confirms the sickness is already inside the village, earlier in the pattern Millhaven finished, but cannot say how it entered or whether stepping in now can change anything, and the captain's spear closes the lane.

beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: Brask's spear across the lane stops the horses and forces the B2 exchange
beats.interiority: the wrongness is quieter than Millhaven because it is still moving, warm bodies instead of silence; she is sure and has nothing to show anyone; two days of road since Millhaven and the same dread arriving on time
beats.plannerWarning: Bread smoke is ambient texture only. The grain answer is not earned until B5; do not let Jaina's attention linger on bread, ovens or flour before then.
beats.continuityNote: This is the place the staff pointed at in Ch3: 'wider, spread out, a stain in a cloth that's been wet through'. The village is the 'alive enough to misunderstand' settlement that Ch3 promised, so B1 pays that off and does not set it up from scratch. Her sense of the contamination is established (late drag in the pulse, old-coin taste, the staff crystal clicking), so it gets one callback anchor and no re-explanation. Four horses where there were seven: the gaps in the line are a callback (Ch3 B11) and need no new image. Hands still wrapped. Jaina has not been inside her own head on the page since Ch2, so her Ch3 actions can surface as memory, but the ride itself gets no recap.
beats.povNote: Jaina can feel the contamination (unlike the elves), so B1's wrongness is legal through her directly. Open on the sensation against the noise, not on the landscape.
beats.verifierModification: Added time anchor, tension, continuity annotation and the open-on-sensation note.

beats.goal: Get the captain to let the party through to the sick without a panic and without Jaina having to talk him down herself.
beats.conflict: Brask has no reason to trust armed outsiders in the middle of an outbreak. Pushed too hard he fights; pushed too soft he stonewalls. Jaina's instinct is to explain the necromancy, which would frighten the street.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas makes Millhaven concrete enough to frighten him without sparking panic, and he gives them room; Jaina gets the access but is left refiling the ranger and annoyed she could not have done it.

beats.valueShift: Sylvanas as escort muscle -> Sylvanas as a skill Jaina lacks
newOnPageInformation: Brask yields because Sylvanas knows exactly how hard to press
The word Millhaven lands on him
Sylvanas takes the village to read while Jaina goes to the sick
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether this village is following Millhaven's full pattern
Whether Brask can keep order if panic starts
sensoryAnchors: work-rough hands on a spear shaft
Sylvanas lowering her voice instead of raising it
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: with the lane open, Jaina walks straight to the infirmary while Sylvanas and Cyndia turn into the village
beats.interiority: could not have done that, and is annoyed she couldn't; had the ranger filed as escort muscle and has to refile her; she would have explained the necromancy to him, at length, which is worse than a spear; how did Sylvanas know how hard to press, and can it be learned
beats.plannerWarning: Dialogue is the writer's. Brask's register per brask-voice.md: short sentences joined by 'and', repeats the one word that hits him ('Millhaven.'). Do not use his 'sold barley' sample (grain pre-signal). Sylvanas's persuasion is a pressure technique, not a speech. Jaina's narration calls her 'Windrunner' here; the slide to 'Sylvanas' comes later in the chapter.
beats.continuityNote: Brask is new. Millhaven is a callback: Sylvanas makes it concrete with things she saw (laid tables, no bodies, the cradle with no baby, sixty walked north), which Jaina also saw. The refiling is not a reset. In Ch2 Jaina already dropped 'talking small' after Sylvanas read the map backward. What she still underrates is Sylvanas's read of people: fear, authority, how hard to press. B2's annoyance is about that new category, and the map is not re-litigated. Brask's address per voice sheet: 'my lady' to Sylvanas until corrected, then 'Ranger-General'; 'miss' to Jaina.
continuityCorrections: Planner warning said Jaina narration uses 'the ranger'. Memory shows her narration name is 'Windrunner'. 'The ranger' in the outline's Inside line is fine as a phrase in thought, but the narration tag stays 'Windrunner' here.
beats.povNote: Agency risk: Jaina watches while Sylvanas acts. Her agency in B2 is the withheld impulse (the necromancy lecture she does not give) and the refiling. Keep that interior active.
beats.verifierModification: Corrected the narration-name rule ('Windrunner', not 'the ranger'); flagged Brask's barley line as a grain pre-signal; framed the refiling as a new category, not a reset of Ch2.

beats.goal: Work out what the sickness is doing in living bodies and narrow the entry route.
beats.conflict: The medic has treated fever because he has no frame for worse. Beds are packed too close, the cases differ in stage, and the wrongness in warm tissue is harder to isolate than in the dead.

outcome.summary: She finds the same necromantic pattern as Millhaven, still moving through living tissue, with the earliest cases clustered in the gut; the route narrows to something people take in, but food, water and contact are still open.

beats.continuityNote: Evolution from the doe (Ch2: contamination in blood, meat, liver and lungs before death, 'running through the tissue like roots in a pot') to living people. The sick-sweet breath is a callback to the girl's 'pears gone brown', and Jaina is the one who asked 'before or after' (Ch3). Here she smells it herself on the earliest cases. It stays a symptom, not a route. Reads go through spell light and the staff, not a bare palm (Ch3 ban, hands wrapped).

scenes.title: The Answer Comes Together
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina and Sylvanas solve different halves of the outbreak until the grain route becomes clear.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Afternoon. Jaina has narrowed the route to something people take in, with water, food and contact all still open. Lyriel is in the infirmary with her, and Sylvanas and Cyndia are out in the village as a pair. No one has named grain. The granary keeper is one of Sylvanas's sources, off Jaina's page until the two halves are compared in B7.
scenes.arcPressure: This is the scene where the two methods prove neither works alone. Jaina must stop treating Sylvanas's read as background.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only (plague-mechanism.md: grain carries the outer shell, strong signature, survives storage, baking and travel; repeated ingestion conditions the body; Jaina's ladder at Ch 4-6 is ingestion, repeated exposure, body participation, still missing the final step). The farmer's-wife and child details come from the outline. No web search run.

beats.goal: Hold the worst cases with stabilization wards while she hunts for what the patients share.
beats.conflict: The wards only buy time and drain her; the village keeps swallowing the source and she cannot out-heal an open tap. Her hands are full, one holding the ward, so even tying a dressing is awkward.

outcome.summary: The wards steady the early cases, a farmer's wife goes still, and Lyriel teaches her the one-handed knot; but relief is only partial and the source stays unnamed, so she starts comparing symptoms to diet and routine instead of reaching for a cleaner spell.

beats.valueShift: magic as the answer -> magic as time bought

beats.transitionIntent: planted question: if it is diet and routine, the pattern should show in who is sickest
beats.interiority: the knot is a small useful thing and she is annoyed at how much she wants it; tying with a ward in the other hand shouldn't be this hard; patching mistakes sounds like Lyriel's kind of joke; the wards hold and that is not the same as a cure
beats.plannerWarning: Keep Lyriel's lesson as short imperatives in order, then she stops talking so Jaina can try (lyriel-voice.md). The fixed line is 'We learn it so we can patch our own mistakes.' The steps: loop over the thumb, wrist under, pull the tail through, set with the teeth. Lyriel's switch to 'Jaina' (from 'Lady Proudmoore') should land in this exchange. Do not narrate the knot as a lesson about trust.
beats.continuityNote: Lyriel last addressed her as 'Lady Proudmoore' in Ch2 and has not addressed her on the page since. Ch3 was all hands (the cheekpiece, two fingers through the cheek-strap while she slept, the far stirrup). The switch to 'Jaina' lands here; she is the only ranger who uses the first name. The one-handed knot is grounded in the hands: one wrapped and raw, one unreliable, one holding a ward. Lyriel's quick hands over Jaina's go over linen wrappings. Jaina's interior vocabulary is nautical, and she is a lord admiral's daughter who knows knots, just not this one. That is a resource for the writer, not a requirement.
beats.verifierModification: Added the hands and the Lyriel address history; transition label normalized.

beats.goal: Find the pattern in who is sickest and what separates them.
beats.conflict: The comfortable answers (water, a shared well, contact) fit some cases and fail others, and she must resist stopping at the first thing that fits.

outcome.summary: The worst cases are the heaviest bread-eaters; people on separate oats or their own provisions are less sick. Repeated meals matter more than one bad swallow. She earns the grain answer from the bodies, but has only the body-side truth, not the road-side source.

beats.interiority: the pleasure of it clicking, in a room full of fevers; earned from the bodies in the right order, proud of that, and ashamed of being proud; bread, so who bakes, who mills, who sells; no, slower, the oat-eaters first, rule out the comfortable answer; the road half still missing, and Sylvanas out there with it
beats.plannerWarning: Grain is earned here and only here; B1 to B4 must not have pre-signalled it. Interiority is argument-in-progress, not a finished conclusion. Differentiate the Millhaven granary 'loudness' from Ch3 (Jaina refused to crown the granary there); callback to that refusal is allowed, as a reason she distrusts a clean answer, not as proof.
beats.continuityNote: The grain answer is new and earned here. Three continuity guards apply. (1) Ch3 method callback: she refused to crown the Millhaven storehouse as origin because 'a store is where things end up'. That is why she distrusts a clean answer, not earlier proof. (2) Water: memory has the contamination in Millhaven's well water and soil. Ruling water out here means water does not separate the sick from the less sick, because everyone drinks from the same well. It does not mean the water is clean. The horses drank Lordaeron water all the way south and read clean, which is consistent and is there if she wants it. (3) Oats are grain too. What separates the patients is this bread, this flour, so the answer is a particular stock, not grain as a category. That precision is what makes the supplier half fit in B7.
continuityCorrections: Ruling out water must not contradict the established contamination of well water and soil (world/magic, contamination-left-the-lines): the claim is that water does not explain the gradient.
The oat-eaters being less sick narrows it to a stock or flour, not to grain in general.
beats.verifierModification: Added the water and oats logic guards; retyped transition and kept the narration name consistent.

beats.decision: She stays at the cots and keeps the wards up, and lets Sylvanas work.

scenes.title: The Granary
scenes.sceneFunction: The village investigation turns into an active hunt inside the grain stores, and the village is saved.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Dusk. Grain, meaning the new supplier's stock, is the carrier, and the granary is where they can prove it. Jaina's stabilization wards are set and left standing over the worst cases while she goes; they weaken without her. The party moves on the granary at once.
scenes.arcPressure: The one clean win for the pair: on time, and it holds. Jaina's answer arrives through food, labour, timing and Sylvanas's eye as much as spellwork.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only (brask-voice.md: farmer-soldier, plain rural Lordaeron speech, closes granary and bakery on their word, sends riders after the last flour cart, burns the stock, writes names in his own ledger). The concentrate, the clay vessel and the capture-poison are outline facts with no canon source. No web search run.

beats.goal: Catch whoever is working the granary and keep the evidence intact.
beats.conflict: The young initiate is watching the operation, realizes he is caught and goes for a lamp to burn everything; fire would destroy the proof and the stock.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas stops the fire, Jaina restrains the watcher, and the concentrated liquid shows the poison is made before it reaches the flour; for a moment they hold both a living witness and a fresh crime scene.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch3 ends in Sylvanas's POV on the evening of the first day south: a living farm with smoke, a dog at the gate, a rowan, a lit candle in the gatepost shrine, and a woman who stares at the bows and the mage's hands wrapped in white rags and shuts her door. The staff in the crook of the mage's elbow points past the farm, south, and the dog follows them along the hedge, barking.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Two days' ride later, same four riders: Sylvanas in front, Cyndia left, Lyriel right, Jaina in the middle on the borrowed mare, still a prisoner under the Ch2 terms. Two empty places at the back of the line. Jaina's hands are still wrapped (left raw, right dead since the Ch2 frost-sheet) and hand-reading is banned. She has slept since the saddle-sleep and arrives sharper than she left Millhaven.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: First time inside Jaina since Ch2, and Ch3 showed her only from outside, so her own read of Millhaven is hers to carry in now, without a recap. She knows the girl, the count, the carter's question and the 'wider' reading. Her Ch2 wish to find someone alive was answered by the cellar. She does not know that Sylvanas felt the noon stone or saw the circle on the map, that Sylvanas thought 'Damn her, then' at her refusal, or that Sylvanas is telling herself she follows the trail, not the mage.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough: the staff still pointing south, now at a village with smoke in its chimneys, and the wrongness under ordinary noise. Don't re-run the two days.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch (Sylvanas to Jaina) and a time skip of two days' riding.

craftResearch.findings: The strongest reveals come from recognisable behaviour, not lab work, and a medical clue must be discoverable by a non-specialist. The reader should get each clue when the detective does. Slow down to let the key clue land, then speed up.

craftResearch.topic: Outbreak reasoning by contrast groups (Snow, Broad Street, 1854)
craftResearch.findings: The case was made by who did NOT fall sick: brewery and workhouse workers with their own water stayed well, and an outlier far away who drank the pump's water died. The control group is the proof.

craftResearch.topic: Try-fail cycles and the mid-book win
craftResearch.findings: Yes-but and no-and outcomes keep characters pushing. A clean win mid-book is fine if it changes the status quo and brings new trouble, and the biggest goal stays open until the climax.

craftResearch.topic: Action from a non-fighter's limited POV
craftResearch.findings: In third limited the prose tracks the POV character's attention. Give sensation (weight, sound, breath) over choreography, avoid over-detail, and let the character's background filter what she notices.

pacing.notes: Tension: medium open (B1), a spike at the lane standoff (B2 medium-high), medium in the sickroom (B3-B4), first peak at the click (B5 high), sequel dip (B6 low), quiet hinge (B7 medium-high), action peak (B8-B9 high), a disaster played as stillness (B10 medium-high), then the night with its open question (B11 medium) and the release (B11a low). No run of three high beats. Scene lengths: S1 medium (3 beats, B2 full), S2 long (B4 and B5 full, B6 light), S3 long but uneven inside (B8 full, B9-B10 standard, two sequels). Per the clue research, B5 is the place to slow down.

structure.notes: The opening lands mid-sensation, with the wrongness under the market noise and a spear across the lane inside the beat. The mid-chapter turn is B5, beat 5 of 12 (42%): the body-side click, completed by the B7 join at 58%. The close is a deliberate clean win (outline: 'their one clean win'), kept open by the dead witness, the made concentrate, the unnamed network and the road southwest. Per the try-fail research, a mid-book win works because it changes the status quo: the party now hunts a supply line. Scene/sequel is 9/3 after the B11 split (planner 9/2). That is scene-heavy for a mixed chapter, but acceptable for an investigation-action chapter, since B3 and B6 are short and B10 deflates. Outline beats 11 map to plan beats 12, with outline beat 11 split in two and no merges.

character.notes: Jaina acts in nearly every beat. B2 and B10 are her passive stretches: B2 is fixed by the withheld lecture and the refiling, and B10 is a loss she witnesses. Supporting roles are distinct: Lyriel is the infirmary and the knot (custody pair), Cyndia is Sylvanas's legwork pair and the hands at the prisoner, Brask is authority yielding, the medic is the frame that missed it, and the initiate is the organization's proof. Arc bullets all land (arcLandingMap). The main correction: Jaina's narration name for Sylvanas is 'Windrunner' (memory), not 'the ranger', so the arc is Windrunner to Sylvanas in narration, with 'Ranger-General' kept aloud.

transitions.notes: Labels normalized ('question-pressure' to 'planted question' on B3, B4 and B5). B6 was labelled a sensory carry but described an action; it is now a real carry on the grain dust from distance to close. B10 to B11 is an emotional carryover into the night decision. The new B11 to B11a is an intentional hard cut from night to morning. B11a closes on a planted question (the planner had 'action-continuation'). Cross-scene: B3's narrowed question opens B4's hunt; B7's 'at once' opens the granary at dusk.

continuity.notes: Corrections: Jaina's narration name for Sylvanas (Windrunner, not 'the ranger'); the 'pleasant, forgettable type from before' had no prior description, so the match is now in pattern; Andorhal has never been named on the page and needs an in-world source; Brask's barley sample is a grain pre-signal; ruling out water must not contradict the established well-water contamination; oats are grain, so the answer is this flour; the hands and the hand-reading ban carry over; custody is held through pairs; the wards are left standing during S3.
